about:
Myriad Semiconductor Manufacturing Division is based in Garfield, Arkansas, and has operated since 1983. The company is owned by Bobby Hobbs, who is identified as the owner on the company’s website. Founded over four decades ago, the business was built around serving the semiconductor equipment market with a focus on long-term customer relationships.

The company designs and supplies custom-configured mask aligners for production, research and development, and university teaching environments. It also remanufactures existing Kasper and Quintel mask aligners to extend equipment life. Myriad maintains a large inventory of spare parts for semiconductor processing equipment and provides printed circuit board repair, field service, and training. In addition, the company stocks a variety of electronic, electrical, and mechanical components — including integrated circuits, transistors, capacitors, sensors, and switches — which it sells through an eBay storefront called Myriad Surplus Store.

Myriad serves semiconductor manufacturers, university laboratories, and R&D facilities worldwide. Its mask aligners are used in production lines, research settings, and teaching programs, though specific customer names are not disclosed.

The company states that its business concept centers on building long-term, mutually beneficial relationships and measures success by its longevity. It emphasizes a reputation for quality products and support built over more than 30 years of global service.
